title_en: Export-Import Bank of China v. Guangcai Shiye Investment Group Co., Ltd. and Stone Group Corporation — dispute over loan guarantee contract
ruling_gist_en: Article 60(3) of the former Company Law, which provides that 'directors and managers shall not use the company's assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts,' means that directors and senior management of the company shall not provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts without the company's authorization. The legislative intent of this provision is to prevent major shareholders or controlling shareholders from manipulating the company to engage in related-party transactions with themselves, thereby harming the interests of minority shareholders. This provision does not categorically prohibit the company from providing guarantees for shareholders. For a limited liability company, when the interests of the company's creditors conflict with those of the company's shareholders, priority shall be given to protecting the interests of the company's creditors. A guarantee provided with the company's assets for the debts of the company's shareholders or other individuals, which complies with the company's articles of association and has been approved by the shareholders' meeting or the board of directors, may be deemed valid.
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan guarantee contract; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Beijing; legal person; financial institution; Company Law; validity of company guarantee for shareholders; validity of board resolution; application of Article 60(3) of the Company Law; reversal of judgment; loan contract; guarantee contract; board resolution; loan restructuring; good faith; contract dispute; guarantee; dispute over loan guarantee contract of group company
full_text_en:
【Ruling Summary】

The provision in Article 60(3) of the Company Law (pre-amendment) that "directors and managers shall not use company assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts" is a prohibition against company directors or senior officers providing guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts without company approval. The legislative intent of this provision is to prevent large or controlling shareholders from manipulating the company to engage in connected transactions with themselves, thereby harming the interests of minority shareholders. This provision does not absolutely prohibit the company from providing guarantees for shareholders. As regards a limited liability company, when the interests of the company's creditors conflict with those of the company's shareholders, priority should be given to protecting the interests of the company's creditors. A guarantee provided with company assets for the company's shareholders or other personal debts that complies with the company's articles of association and has been approved by the company's shareholders' meeting or board of directors may be held valid.

Supreme People's Court  
Civil Judgment  

(2006) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 49

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Export-Import Bank, domiciled at No. 77 Beiheyan Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.  
Legal Representative: Li Ruogu, Chairman of the Board of the Bank.  
Agent ad litem: Liu Shijie, lawyer with Beijing Huicheng Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Guangcai Enterprise Investment Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at 8th Floor, Beijing Hotel, No. 33 East Chang'an Street, Dongcheng District, Beijing.  
Legal Representative: Lu Zhiqiang, Chairman of the Board of the Company.  
Agent ad litem: Huang Xiaoyuan, lawyer with Beijing Gonghe Law Firm.  
Agent ad litem: Li Yong, lawyer with Beijing Gonghe Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Stone Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 2 Haidian Street, Haidian District, Beijing.  
Legal Representative: Duan Yongji, Chairman of the Board of the Company.  
Agent ad litem: Zhong Chai, employee of the Company.  
Agent ad litem: Fan Ning, employee of the Company.

The appellant China Export-Import Bank (hereinafter referred to as the Export-Import Bank) appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (2005) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 1182 rendered by the Beijing High People's Court in the case of dispute over a loan guarantee contract involving the appellee Guangcai Enterprise Investment Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Guangcai Group) and the defendant at first instance Stone Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Stone Group). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Adjudicator Fu Jinlian serving as the presiding judge, and Adjudicator Zhang Shuming and Acting Adjudicator Li Jingping as members. Clerk An Yang served as court recorder. The trial of this case has now concluded.

**Facts Found by the Court of First Instance**

On December 25, 2001, the Export-Import Bank and Stone Group entered into a Loan Contract for Export Seller's Credit (2001) Jin Yin Jing (Xin He) Zi No. 11005, under which the Export-Import Bank agreed to provide Stone Group with an export seller's credit facility of RMB 180,000,000 for a term of 13 months. Guangcai Group was to provide a repayment guarantee, such that if Stone Group failed to repay the principal and interest on the loan when due, Guangcai Group would repay the same. Duan Yongji, Chairman of the Board of Stone Group, signed the loan contract on behalf of Stone Group. On the same day, the Export-Import Bank and Guangcai Group entered into a Guarantee Contract (2001) Jin Yin Jing (Xin Bao) Zi No. 11005, under which Guangcai Group agreed to provide joint and several liability guarantee for all debts of Stone Group under the aforesaid loan contract. The guarantee period was two years after the full maturity of all loan principal and interest. In the event of an extension of the loan, the guarantee period would change accordingly. Guangcai Group submitted to the Export-Import Bank a board resolution dated October 23, 2001, resolving to provide a guarantee for Stone Group. The resolution bore the signatures of six persons, including five directors and one representative of a shareholder unit. Duan Yongji, Chairman of the Board of Stone Group, signed the resolution in his capacity as a director of Guangcai Group.

On December 26, 2003, the Export-Import Bank, Stone Group, and Guangcai Group entered into a Loan Restructuring Agreement, which served as an amendment and supplement to the aforesaid Loan Contract for Export Seller's Credit (2001) Jin Yin Jing (Xin He) Zi No. 11005 and the Guarantee Contract (2001) Jin Yin Jing (Xin Bao) Zi No. 11005. The agreement provided that the loan restructuring amount was RMB 160,000,000, with an initial interest rate of 4.23%, to be adjusted annually thereafter in accordance with the loan interest rates prescribed by the People's Bank of China. Stone Group undertook to repay the debts according to the following repayment schedule: RMB 20,000,000 each in June and December 2004, RMB 25,000,000 each in June and December 2005, and RMB 35,000,000 each in June and December 2006. Stone Telecom Co., Ltd. was to provide a piece of real estate in Beijing as mortgage security. Guangcai Group was to provide joint and several liability guarantee for all debts of Stone Group under the restructuring agreement, with the guarantee period commencing from the date of maturity of all debts under the restructuring agreement and lasting for two years. If Stone Group failed to repay the debts and pay interest as agreed, or failed to complete the real estate mortgage procedures by June 30, 2004, the Export-Import Bank had the right to declare all debts immediately due and demand that Stone Group immediately pay all debts in full, and demand that Guangcai Group pay the debts. Duan Yongji, Chairman of the Board of Stone Group, signed the Loan Restructuring Agreement on behalf of Stone Group. Guangcai Group submitted to the Export-Import Bank a board resolution dated November 3, 2003, resolving to provide a guarantee for Stone Group. The resolution stated that Guangcai Group agreed to continue to provide joint and several liability guarantee for repayment of principal and interest on the outstanding loan principal balance of RMB 160,000,000 under the original loan contract (2001) Jin Yin Jing (Xin He) Zi No. 11005. Two directors signed the resolution.

On December 29, 2003, the Export-Import Bank, pursuant to the aforesaid Loan Restructuring Agreement, processed a new loan of RMB 160,000,000 for Stone Group. Stone Telecom Co., Ltd. did not complete the real estate mortgage procedures for the Export-Import Bank. As of September 1, 2005 (the date when the Export-Import Bank filed the lawsuit with the court of first instance), Stone Group had, in accordance with the Loan Restructuring Agreement, repaid the interest on the maturing loans and RMB 24,000,000 of the loan principal, but had not repaid the remaining principal by the agreed deadlines. The Export-Import Bank therefore, in accordance with the terms of the Loan Restructuring Agreement, declared all debts immediately due and filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting that Stone Group and Guangcai Group repay the entire outstanding debt principal of RMB 136,000,000 plus interest. After the Export-Import Bank filed the lawsuit, on September 21, 2005, Stone Group repaid interest of RMB 1,747,416.01.

It was further found that Guangcai Group was established with capital contributions from 11 corporate shareholders, with a registered capital of RMB 500,000,000. Among them, Shandong Fanhai Group Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 356,000,000, representing 71.2% of the capital; Stone Group contributed RMB 1,000,000, representing 0.2%. The board of directors of Guangcai Group consisted of 11 directors, each appointed by a shareholder unit. Lu Zhiqiang, Chairman of the Board of the major shareholder Shandong Fanhai Group Co., Ltd., served as Chairman of the Board of Guangcai Group. The articles of association of Guangcai Group provided that: each board meeting shall be convened by notifying all directors 10 days prior to the meeting, specifying the agenda, location, and time; a board meeting may be convened only if at least two-thirds of the directors are present; voting rights at board meetings are exercised in proportion to capital contributions; directors who are unable to attend may, in writing, entrust another director to attend the meeting and exercise voting rights; board resolutions shall be effective only if passed by directors holding more than two-thirds of the equity; and the minutes and records of each board meeting shall be signed and confirmed by the directors present.

The board resolution of Guangcai Group dated October 23, 2001, resolving to provide a guarantee for Stone Group, bore the signatures of five directors (including Chairman Lu Zhiqiang) and one representative of a shareholder unit. The shareholder units represented by these signatories collectively held 93.6% of the equity in Guangcai Group. The board resolution dated November 3, 2003, resolving to provide a guarantee for Stone Group, bore the signatures of two directors (including Chairman Lu Zhiqiang). The shareholder units represented by these signatories collectively held 91.2% of the equity in Guangcai Group.

**Opinion of the Court of First Instance**

The court of first instance held that the loan relationship set forth in the loan contract concluded between the Export-Import Bank and Stone Group on December 25, 2001, and in the Loan Restructuring Agreement concluded on December 26, 2003, among the Export-Import Bank, Stone Group, and Guangcai Group, represented the true intentions of the Export-Import Bank and Stone Group, and did not violate any mandatory provisions of laws or regulations, and therefore should be found lawful and valid. Stone Group's failure to repay the loan within the time limit agreed in the Loan Restructuring Agreement constituted a breach of contract. The Export-Import Bank was entitled to declare all debts immediately due and demand immediate repayment in full from Stone Group. Stone Group shall repay the Export-Import Bank the outstanding loan principal of RMB 136,000,000 plus the corresponding interest. Since Stone Group repaid interest of RMB 1,747,416.01 on September 21, 2005, this amount shall be deducted from the interest claimed by the Export-Import Bank.

Guangcai Group, by means of a board resolution, decided to provide a joint and several liability guarantee for its shareholder Stone Group, and on December 25, 2001, entered into the Guarantee Contract with the Export-Import Bank, and on December 26, 2003, included guarantee clauses in the Loan Restructuring Agreement with the Export-Import Bank and Stone Group. Pursuant to the mandatory provisions of Article 60(3) of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (pre-amendment) (hereinafter "Company Law (pre-amendment)"), which provides that "directors and managers shall not use company assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts," a company's provision of a guarantee for the company's shareholders requires the consent of the shareholders' meeting or a special provision in the articles of association. Directors have no authority to decide on matters involving the use of company assets to guarantee shareholders. The board of directors, as a corporate organ through which directors collectively exercise their powers, has no authority to decide on the use of company assets to guarantee shareholders, given the absence of any provision in the law authorizing the board to provide external guarantees, and in the absence of authorization from the articles of association or the shareholders' meeting to the board, also by reason of the prohibitory provisions of the law against individual directors. The prohibitory provision of Article 60(3) of the Company Law (pre-amendment) applies both to individual directors and to the board of directors as a whole. Therefore, the act of Guangcai Group in providing a joint and several liability guarantee for its shareholder Stone Group by means of a board resolution was invalid because it violated the mandatory provisions of the Company Law (pre-amendment), and the Guarantee Contract and the guarantee clauses in the Loan Restructuring Agreement were also invalid. Guangcai Group shall bear fault liability for the invalidity of the guarantee contract.

Duan Yongji, Chairman of the Board of Stone Group, signed the loan contract and the Loan Restructuring Agreement on behalf of Stone Group. He also signed the board resolution of Guangcai Group dated October 23, 2001, which was submitted by Guangcai Group to the Export-Import Bank, as a director of Guangcai Group. Therefore, it should be found that when the Export-Import Bank accepted the guarantee from Guangcai Group, it was aware of the fact that the borrower Stone Group was a shareholder of the guarantor Guangcai Group. Accordingly, under the circumstances where the law expressly prohibited directors from using company assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders, the Export-Import Bank nevertheless accepted the guarantee provided by Guangcai Group for its shareholder Stone Group, and therefore also had fault regarding the invalidity of the Guarantee Contract and the guarantee clauses. Pursuant to Article 7 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, Guangcai Group shall bear liability to the Export-Import Bank for one-half of the portion of Stone Group's debts that Stone Group fails to repay.

The shareholders' meeting is the company's supreme authority, and the board of directors is the company's management decision-making body. According to the articles of association of Guangcai Group, they have different functions. The board meeting of Guangcai Group held on November 3, 2003, to decide on providing a joint and several guarantee for Stone Group, had a number of directors attending that did not meet the minimum quorum requirement stipulated in the articles of association of Guangcai Group for convening a board meeting, constituting a serious procedural defect. From a procedural standpoint, the board resolution so formed should also be invalid. Therefore, even if the composition of the board of directors of Guangcai Group overlapped with that of the shareholders' meeting, it cannot be inferred that Guangcai Group's provision of a guarantee for its shareholder was approved by the shareholders' meeting. Accordingly, the Export-Import Bank's claim that the board resolution and the guarantee clauses were valid was not supported. The court, in accordance with Articles 206 and 207 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 60(3) of the Company Law (pre-amendment), and Articles 4, 7, and 9 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Stone Group shall, within 10 days after the effective date of this judgment, repay the Export-Import Bank the loan principal of RMB 136,000,000 plus interest (calculated from September 1, 2005, until the date of full repayment, based on the principal of RMB 136,000,000, at the annual interest rate of 4.23% as agreed in the Loan Restructuring Agreement, deducting the interest of RMB 1,747,416.01 repaid by Stone Group on September 21, 2005); 2. The guarantee clauses in the Loan Restructuring Agreement entered into among the Export-Import Bank, Stone Group, and Guangcai Group are invalid; 3. Guangcai Group shall bear liability for compensation in the amount of one-half of the portion of the debts set forth in paragraph 1 above that Stone Group fails to repay. After bearing the compensation liability, Guangcai Group has the right to recover from Stone Group. The case acceptance fee of RMB 690,010 and the property preservation fee of RMB 680,520, totaling RMB 1,370,530, shall be borne by Stone Group, and Guangcai Group shall bear joint and several liability for one-half of the said case acceptance fee and property preservation fee.

The Export-Import Bank, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the court of first instance, appealed to this Court, stating: 1. The Company Law (pre-amendment) does not expressly prohibit a company from providing guarantees for its shareholders. The guarantee provided by Guangcai Group for Stone Group does not violate any prohibitory provision of the law and is therefore valid. The content of the board resolution or shareholders' meeting resolution of Guangcai Group does not violate the Company Law or the articles of association of the company and is also lawful and valid. The court of first instance found that the board of directors of Guangcai Group had no authority to provide a guarantee for the company's shareholder and that the board resolution was invalid, without first determining whether the board of directors' decision to provide a guarantee for the company's shareholder violated the company's articles of association. Such finding lacks legal basis. 2. The members of the board of directors of Guangcai Group and the members of the shareholders' meeting overlap in composition and are substantially identical. The functions of the board of directors as set out in the articles of association overlap with those of the shareholders' meeting and are functionally the same. When the company's shareholders' meeting established the articles of association, it authorized the board of directors to exercise the powers of the shareholders' meeting, and the shareholders' meeting has the legal characteristics of having expressly authorized and ratified the board's resolution. Therefore, the legal effect of the board resolution is equivalent to that of a shareholders' meeting resolution. 3. The Export-Import Bank did not receive the board resolution of Guangcai Group dated October 23, 2001, which bore the signature of Duan Yongji as a director of Guangcai Group. The court of first instance found that Guangcai Group submitted this resolution when providing the guarantee for Stone Group, and based on that, found that the Export-Import Bank knew that Stone Group was a shareholder of Guangcai Group, inferring that the Export-Import Bank had fault liability. There is no factual basis for such finding. The Export-Import Bank requests that the second item of the original judgment be set aside on appeal, and that Guangcai Group be ordered to bear joint and several liability for Stone Group's debts in this case.

The appellee Guangcai Group argued in its defense: 1. The act of Guangcai Group in providing a joint and several liability guarantee for its shareholder Stone Group by means of a board resolution is invalid because it violates the prohibitory provisions of the Company Law (pre-amendment). 2. In the absence of authorization from the shareholders' meeting of Guangcai Group, the board of directors of the company has no authority to decide on the use of company assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders. The shareholders' meeting and the board of directors differ in their functions, convening procedures, and composition. The fact that the legal representatives of shareholder units and the company's directors are the same persons cannot lead to the inference that a board resolution is equivalent to a shareholders' meeting resolution or that the shareholders' meeting has expressly authorized or ratified the board's resolution. The board resolution involved in this case to provide a guarantee for Stone Group violated the convening procedures prescribed in the company's articles of association and should be held invalid. 3. The Export-Import Bank, knowing that Stone Group was a shareholder of Guangcai Group and that the law prohibits a company from providing guarantees for its shareholders, nevertheless accepted the guarantee provided by Guangcai Group. It bears fault for the invalidity of the Guarantee Contract and the guarantee clauses in the Loan Restructuring Agreement and shall bear corresponding liability in accordance with the law. The court of first instance correctly found the facts and applied the law. The Export-Import Bank's appeal should be dismissed and the original judgment affirmed.

The defendant at first instance, Stone Group, did not submit a written defense. During the second-instance cross-examination before this Court, it stated that it agreed with the defense of the appellee Guangcai Group and expressed no objection to the principal and interest determined in the original judgment as owed by Stone Group.

During the second-instance proceedings before this Court, the Export-Import Bank stated that it did not receive the board resolution of Guangcai Group dated December 25, 2001, which bore the signature of Duan Yongji, Chairman of Stone Group, as a director of Guangcai Group, and that it was unaware that Stone Group was a shareholder of Guangcai Group. Guangcai Group also had no evidence to prove that it had delivered this resolution to the Export-Import Bank. Therefore, this Court does not find this fact. Except for the above, this Court confirms the other facts found by the court of first instance.

**Opinion of the Court**

Stone Group is the principal debtor under the loan contract in this case. It failed to repay the Export-Import Bank's loan in accordance with the contract. The Export-Import Bank is entitled, as agreed, to declare all loans immediately due. Stone Group had no objection during the second-instance proceedings to the principal and interest determined in the original judgment, so the first item of the original judgment should be affirmed.

The guarantee provided by Guangcai Group for Stone Group's debts in this case occurred before the amendment of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. Therefore, this case shall be governed by the Company Law (pre-amendment), the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 60(3) of the Company Law (pre-amendment) provides: "Directors and managers shall not use company assets to provide guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts." This provision is a prohibitory rule against company directors and senior officers providing guarantees for the company's shareholders or other personal debts without company approval. However, this provision does not absolutely prohibit the company from providing guarantees for shareholders. For a limited liability company, the Company Law (pre-amendment) does not expressly prohibit the company from providing related-party guarantees in its own name, provided that such guarantees comply with the company's articles of association and have been approved by the company's shareholders' meeting or board of directors. The legislative purpose of the above provision is to prevent large or controlling shareholders from manipulating the company into engaging in connected transactions with themselves, thereby harming the interests of minority shareholders, and to uphold the principle of capital maintenance and protect the rights and interests of minority shareholders. The provision does not prohibit or restrict the use of company assets to provide guarantees for minority shareholders where such guarantees have been approved by the company's shareholders' meeting or board of directors. From a value orientation perspective, when balancing the conflict of interests between company creditors and company shareholders, priority should be given to protecting the interests of company creditors.

According to the facts found in this case, Guangcai Group Company, as a limited liability company, had a registered capital of RMB 500 million, of which Shandong Fanhai Group Company contributed RMB 356 million, accounting for 71.2% of the capital contribution; Weifang Baoshun Construction Co., Ltd. contributed RMB 100 million, accounting for 20%; Stone Group contributed RMB 1 million, accounting for 0.2%. Its articles of association did not stipulate that the company could not provide guarantees for its shareholders. The articles of association provided that the board of directors is the legal organ of the company, the members of the board of directors are appointed by the shareholder units, and the voting procedure of the board of directors adopts the form of capital majority rule. Among the 11 shareholders of the company, the legal representatives of 10 shareholder units were appointed as directors of the company, and one was a representative of a shareholder unit. The evidence provided by Guangcai Group showed that at the two board meetings held on December 25, 2001, and December 26, 2003, where the company agreed to provide a guarantee for Stone Group, directors holding 93.6% and 91.2% of the company's equity, respectively, agreed to provide the guarantee for Stone Group, which complied with the provisions of the articles of association. The board resolutions were affixed with the seal of the board of directors, and the seal of Guangcai Group was affixed to the "Guarantee Contract" and the "Loan Restructuring Agreement". Guangcai Group did not dispute the authenticity of the above seals. It should be determined that the execution of the above "Guarantee Contract" and "Loan Restructuring Agreement" by Guangcai Group represented its true intention, did not contravene the will of the vast majority of shareholders holding capital, and this guarantee act also did not violate the prohibitive provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and should be valid. Regarding Guangcai Group's argument that, according to the company's articles of association, at least eight directors must attend a board meeting for it to be convened, but the above two board resolutions were signed by only five and two directors respectively, thus the board meetings were invalidly convened and the board resolutions were invalid, this Court holds that: the fact that five and two directors respectively signed the board resolutions does not prove that only five or two directors attended the board meetings. Guangcai Group bears the burden of proof to show that the convening of the two board meetings of the company on December 25, 2001, and December 26, 2003, complied with the director attendance requirements stipulated in the articles of association, but the company has never provided the minutes or original records of the two meetings, and therefore should bear the consequences of failure to adduce evidence. Moreover, even if there were defects in the board resolutions, such defects are internal corporate acts and cannot affect the validity of the company's external guarantee acts. Therefore, Guangcai Group's claims in this lawsuit that the board resolutions were invalid and that the company's guarantee for its shareholder was invalid lack factual and legal basis and violate the rule against estoppel in civil litigation, so this Court does not support them. The Export-Import Bank's ground of appeal that Guangcai Group's provision of a guarantee for Stone Group did not violate the prohibitive provisions of law, that it was a valid guarantee, and that Guangcai Group should bear joint and several liability for Stone Group's debts in this case is established, and this Court supports it.

In summary, the facts found in the original judgment are basically clear, but the application of law was erroneous, and the determination of liability was improper, which should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby adjudicates as follows:

1. Affirm Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment (2005) Gao Min Chu Zi No. 1182 of the Beijing High People's Court;

2. Set aside Item 2 of the main text of the said civil judgment;

3. Amend Item 3 of the main text of the said civil judgment to: Guangcai Enterprise Investment Group Co., Ltd. shall bear joint and several suretyship liability for the above debts of Stone Group Company. After bearing joint and several suretyship liability, Guangcai Enterprise Investment Group Co., Ltd. has the right to seek recourse from Stone Group Company.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 690,010, and the property preservation fee is RMB 680,520, totaling RMB 1,370,530, to be borne by Stone Group Company; the court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 690,010, to be borne by Guangcai Enterprise Investment Group Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Fu Jinlian

Judge: Zhang Shuming

Acting Judge: Li Jingping

Clerk: An Yang
